items.claim: ReserveWarehouseStock is dispatched inside DB::transaction() with no after-commit (plain ShouldQueue, connection after_commit false), so a worker can run it before the order and its lines are committed, or for an order that was rolled back. May be reported at the job class (app/Jobs/ReserveWarehouseStock.php) instead.
AwardLoyaltyPoints increments loyalty_points before the CRM call; if the CRM call throws, the job is retried (tries 4) and the points are added again.
BuildSalesExport has $timeout = 300 on the redis connection whose retry_after is 180 (config/queue.php:26), so a long export is handed to a second worker while the first is still running.

SendAbandonedCartReminder serialises the Cart model (SerializesModels) and runs 3 hours later, but checkout deletes the cart, so the job fails with ModelNotFoundException (no $deleteWhenMissingModels or missing-cart check).
SyncProductToSearchIndex implements ShouldBeUnique without uniqueId(), so the lock is per class: while one product's sync is queued, syncs for every other product are silently dropped.
PushContactToMailchimp uses RateLimited('mailchimp') but no limiter with that name is registered (AppServiceProvider registers 'mailchimp-api'), so the job is not rate limited at all.
SendOrderConfirmation is dispatched inside the transaction, so it can run before commit or after a rollback.
IssueReturnRefund can refund twice when it is retried or runs twice.
items.why_fine: It skips returns already refunded and passes a stable idempotency key that the gateway honours.

items.claim: ArchiveOldOrders has $timeout = 900, longer than the queue's retry_after, so it can run twice at once.
items.why_fine: It runs on the redis-long connection with retry_after 1000.

items.claim: SendReviewReplyNotification fails with ModelNotFoundException if the review is deleted before it runs.
items.why_fine: $deleteWhenMissingModels = true is declared as the property default.

items.claim: RecalculateCustomerSegment is a unique job whose key or lock expiry is wrong (missing uniqueId or uniqueFor).
items.why_fine: It has uniqueId() returning the customer id and uniqueFor 900.

items.claim: GeocodeCustomerAddress's RateLimited('geocoding') limiter is undefined, or its releases exhaust the job's tries.
items.why_fine: The 'geocoding' limiter is registered and the job is bounded by retryUntil().

items.claim: ProductObserver dispatches from model events, so the job is queued inside the caller's transaction.
